text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran the new reranker (v3b-quant) bringup on the short-doc benchmark and seeing weird behavior: NDCG almost flat vs baseline but Hit@1 drops ~6% for docs < 120 tokens. looks like a length bias after quant.

devon: interesting. is this across all datasets or just the short-doc split? any difference by candidate ordering? :thinking_face:

maria: just the short-doc split (we stratified by doc_len). long-doc and mid-doc mostly fine. candidate ordering was randomized. bucket sizes: <120, 120-600, >600.

alex: can you paste the eval command you used? want to re-run locally and check tokenizer/truncation.

maria: sure — here's the harness call:

```
./eval_rerank.py \
  --model v3b-quant \
  --candidates candidates.jsonl \
  --queries queries_short.jsonl \
  --tokenizer redwood-tokenizer \
  --truncate_to 128 \
  --batch 64 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output /tmp/v3b-quant-short.jsonl
```

sasha: two quick checks: 1) verify tokenization parity vs baseline (int8 quant can change tokenization if using different libs), 2) confirm prefix priming was identical — are you sending the same prompt template for short vs long?

maria: tokenizer should be identical (same tokenizer binary) but i'll double-check the binary hash. prompt template is same except we use different context concatenation for long docs (we add a snippet header). short docs used direct doc text.

devon: try rerunning with truncate_to 256 (so you avoid edge truncation) and also run with deterministic candidate sort (by id) to remove ordering flakiness.

maria: doing that now. also re-running with float baseline (v3b-fp16) to confirm quant delta.

(eval-bot): job 6332110001 finished: v3b-quant short-doc run complete — uploaded /tmp/v3b-quant-short.jsonl

maria: results quick scan: v3b-fp16 Hit@1 = 0.68, v3b-quant Hit@1 = 0.62; NDCG@10 0.79 vs 0.78 (tiny). so rank quality seems roughly preserved but top-1 degenerates.

alex: that pattern smells like calibration/score compression. quant reduces score spread leading to ties/near-ties at top rank. do you have score histograms? also check softmax temperature or rescoring scale.

maria: attaching quick histogram (pasted):

- fp16 scores mean 1.12 std 0.34
- quant scores mean 0.98 std 0.18

sasha: exactly — std collapses. For rerankers we normally apply a learned rescale layer (logit_scale) during training/inference. is that being applied for the quant build? sometimes ONNX export/quant skips a final scale.

maria: good call. the export script has an option --fold_scale True/False. i think we folded it in the fp16 export but not in quant. will re-export with fold_scale enabled.

devon: while you're at it, run a tiny ablation: (A) fold_scale on, (B) apply post-hoc temperature (0.8,1.0,1.2), (C) rerun with deterministic candidate order and truncate_to 256. that'll tell whether it's scale vs trunc.

maria: plan accepted. running A/B/C now. also bumping seed multiples.

(eval-bot): job 6332110105 finished: A/B/C sweep. outputs: /tmp/quant-sweep/*.jsonl

maria: quick summary:
- A (fold_scale=True): Hit@1 = 0.69 (fixes it), NDCG@10 = 0.79
- B (temp=0.8/1.2): small changes, best at 0.95 of baseline
- C (det order + truncate 256): no major difference

alex: so safe to conclude export missed scale in quant path. that's a regression vector for future ONNX quant pipelines. we should add a test in the model-onboard checklist that checks score std and topk hit against float baseline.

sasha: agree. propose CI test: run 1000-sample short-doc cohort, assert Hit@1 >= baseline - 0.02 and std(scores) >= 0.25 or rescale applied.

maria: i'll open a PR that: re-exports quant with fold_scale, adds a short-doc smoke eval job, and records a note in the onboarding doc about this pitfall. @devon @alex any objections?

devon: go for it. maybe also add a debug flag that prints the final linear layer weights hash so we can detect folded vs non-folded exports.

maria: good idea. will add.

alex: thanks for triage! saved us from shipping a weird top1 regression. :tada:

sasha: short follow-up: can we add a small calibration retrain (one epoch) for quant variants in future onboarding to recover any residual scale mismatch? just a note.

maria: noted. i'll add it to the onboarding checklist as optional step. closing thread after PR lands.

devon: thx — ping when PR is up.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/compare/PR-324 — includes fold_scale fix + eval smoke. will monitor tomorrow's scheduled bench. :shipit!
